title: Kegworth air disaster
summary: A British Midland Airways Boeing 737-400 experienced a left engine fan blade fracture during climb. Smoke entered the cabin, and the crew incorrectly identified the right engine as the source based on outdated knowledge of the 737 ventilation system. They shut down the functioning right engine. Fire subsequently developed in the left engine during descent. The aircraft crashed onto a motorway embankment near Kegworth, killing 47 of 126 on board.
probable_cause: A fan blade fracture in the left engine caused smoke and vibration. The crew misidentified the engine due to unfamiliarity with 737-400 ventilation differences and shut down the functioning right engine. Fire in the left engine during descent led to loss of control and crash.

title: Independent Air 1851
summary: Independent Air Flight 1851 struck Pico Alto mountain on approach to Santa Maria Airport in the Azores on February 8, 1989. During descent, the trainee air traffic controller transmitted an incorrect QNH that was 9 hPa too high. The crew misheard due to non-standard phraseology and used the wrong altimeter setting. The aircraft descended below safe altitude and struck the mountain, killing all 144 aboard.
probable_cause: During the transmission, the trainee controller transmitted an incorrect QNH that was 9 hPa too high and used non-standard terminology. The crew did not fully hear the approach instructions and misheard the pressure setting, leading them to descend below safe altitude. The crew's failure to question the high pressure reading contributed to the accident.

The crew misunderstood ATC clearance due to ambiguous radio phraseology with multiple identically-coded beacons and abbreviations creating confusion. The captain misinterpreted descent to 2400 feet as descent to 400 feet. Multiple ground proximity warnings were issued and completely ignored by the crew leading to controlled flight into terrain.

title: United Airlines 811
summary: United Airlines Flight 811, a Boeing 747-122, experienced cargo door failure in flight on 24 February 1989 shortly after climbing out of Honolulu. The forward cargo door separated, causing explosive decompression that ejected 9 passengers and 1 flight attendant almost blown out. The aircraft was damaged including engines 3 and 4 which experienced heavy vibration. The flight crew performed an emergency descent and 180-degree turn to return to Honolulu, where the aircraft landed safely without further incident.
probable_cause: The cargo door opened in flight due to malfunction of the electrical system combined with deficiencies in the door's latching mechanism design. The door latch arms were inadequately designed, and the electrical system failure caused the door to open at altitude.

title: Interflug 102
summary: An Ilyushin Il-62M on takeoff from Berlin Schönefeld was cleared for runway 25L. At rotation speed the crew pulled on the yoke but the aircraft did not respond. title: United Airlines 232

location.name: Sioux Gateway Airport, Sioux City, Iowa

summary: McDonnell Douglas DC-10 suffered catastrophic failure of its tail-mounted engine due to unnoticed manufacturing defect in the engine fan disk. The fan disk failure resulted in total loss of all three independent hydraulic flight control systems. The crew, with assistance from a company check pilot passenger, was able to control the aircraft using only engine thrust and land it at Sioux City. Despite the extreme difficulty of an aircraft with no hydraulic controls, the crew executed an emergency landing on a closed runway. Of 296 people on board, 111 died while 185 survived, making this crash considered a success due to superior crew resource management.
probable_cause: An undetected manufacturing defect in the number 2 engine's fan disk caused catastrophic disk failure. The failure resulted in severing all three independent hydraulic systems, creating a condition for which the aircraft was not designed. The DC-10 design assumed no single failure could cause loss of multiple hydraulic systems. The crew's exceptional resource management and decision to land at Sioux City saved the majority of occupants.

events.text: Flight 203 took off as scheduled at 07:13 from El Dorado International Airport in Bogotá.
Five minutes into the flight, at a speed of 794 km/h and an altitude of 13000 ft, an explosive charge detonated.

title: United Express 2415
summary: United Express Flight 2415 crashed 400 feet short of runway 21R at Tri-Cities Airport on December 26, 1989, during final approach. The aircraft had accumulated airframe icing after the captain declined de-icing at Yakima, and slowed to 110 knots while descending steeply. The combination of icing, low speed, and excessive descent rate resulted in loss of control.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determined that the combination of airframe icing, failure to obtain ground de-icing, low airspeed, and excessive descent rate resulted in loss of control of the aircraft during approach.

factors.evidence: Captain Roberts declined de-icing at Yakima despite offers
